## Q4-2025 Earnings Call

### AI Summary Earnings Call on Feb 12, 2026

![](https://ik.imagekit.io/kkbzr2uz4cp/stock/krx/352820.png?tr=w-200)

This growth was driven by strong global demand, successful artist comebacks, and expansion across genres and regions. Despite a stagnant album market, HYBE maintained approximately 30% market share in album sales.

Operating profit fell to KRW 49.9 billion with a margin of just 1.9%. The decline was mainly due to upfront investments in debuting new artists globally and restructuring costs in the US business. Management explained these costs are expected to support better mid-to-long-term profitability.

HYBE artists held 279 large-scale global concerts in 2025. Key acts like SEVENTEEN, TXT, ENHYPEN, and new groups such as CORTIS and KATSEYE all delivered strong performances, both in sales and audience mobilization. HYBE's influence expanded in regions including Korea, Japan, Latin America, and North America.

BTS will complete military service by June 2025 and return with a new album ('ARIRANG') and a historic world tour, including at least 82 shows in 34 cities. This is expected to drive major growth for HYBE in 2026, with BTS activities anticipated to boost both revenue and platform engagement.

Unique promotional and production strategies contributed to this success. HYBE is transitioning its US operations to a label-based model, incurring KRW 200 billion in non-cash impairment losses in Q4 2025. The stories that a teenage group can share and high-quality content that reflect their genuine sincerity have resonated with listeners, creating a momentum for extended life of their music and sustainable value creation. Their unique and original identity has made a great appeal to diverse global industries beyond music.

They also carried out cross-genre collaborations, including sports, gaming and film. CORTIS was invited to sing a new original soundtrack for a major Hollywood animation. One of the tracks in their debut album titled Go was used as a soundtrack for popular game NBA 2026 Season 4.

This rapid growth is the result of the vision of BigHit Music, a label within HYBE Music Group to provide the best musical experience by respecting artist creativity and actively supporting their creative activities.

Global strategy, performance growth drive sales despite structural investments, one-time costs

[OSEN=Jang Woo-young reporter] HYBE recorded annual sales that increased by approximately 18% compared to the previous year, setting a new record high since its founding. The "multi-home, multi-genre" strategy targeting global markets and strong sales growth in the performance sector drove the expansion. Operating profits decreased compared to the previous year as costs for structural improvements, including preemptive investments for mid- to long-term growth and revenue structure reforms, were reflected.

HYBE's consolidated revenue for 2025 was 2.6499 trillion Korean won, with performance sector achievements driving growth. Last year, HYBE successfully held a total of 279 global performances (250 concerts and 29 fan meetings), resulting in sales of 763.9 billion Korean won in the performance sector, an increase of approximately 69% compared to the previous year.

Building on this box office success, HYBE rose five spots to rank fourth globally in the "Top Promoters" category of Billboard's "2025 Boxscore Annual Report," entering the "Big 4." Among the four K-pop artists who entered Billboard's "2025 Top Tours," three teams (Jay Hop, Seventeen, and Enhypen) were counted as HYBE Music Group artists, reaffirming the company's strong IP (intellectual property) power.

In 2025, HYBE maintained a solid influence within the market despite an overall adjustment trend in the album market. Annual cumulative sales based on Circle Chart were approximately 19.6 million units, with a market share of about 30%. The annual streaming count for HYBE Music Group artists reached a total of 3.7 billion times, with a 3% share based on the "Global Spotify 200." In 2025, audio sources accounted for approximately 37% of HYBE's total album sales revenue.

The global super-fan platform Weverse achieved annual profitability through revenue structure reforms and operational efficiency improvements. Diversification of revenue through expanded artist participation, enhanced e-commerce operations, and digital business expansion contributed to strong performance. This year, performance is expected to further improve with the resumption of BTS team activities and growth in e-commerce and digital businesses.

Consolidated operating profits for 2025 were 49.9 billion Korean won, a decrease of approximately 73% compared to the previous year. The decline in operating profits was influenced by initial investment costs for new artist debuts and one-time costs during business structure reorganization.

First, artists such as Japan's aoen, South Korea's CORTIS, and Latin America's SANTOS BRAVOS debuted in large numbers, concentrating initial costs. These artists are growing into core IPs in their respective regions. aoen topped the Oricon Daily Chart with their debut single "The Blue Sun," while CORTIS achieved million-seller status in their debut year. SANTOS BRAVOS' debut concert, with a capacity of 10,000 seats, sold out, and an additional 70,000 viewers watched the performance online.

One-time costs related to operational efficiency improvements in the business structure were also reflected. HYBE is restructuring its business to mitigate volatility in the existing management-centric structure in North America and transition to a label-centric IP business model. As a result of conservatively re-evaluating the appropriateness of asset values in line with the changed business structure, an impairment loss of approximately 200 billion Korean won was recognized as non-operating loss in the management business sector during the fourth quarter of last year. This is an accounting loss with no actual cash outflow. This measure aims to enhance accounting transparency and predictability. Considering the strengthened fundamentals of HYBE America, the risk of additional large-scale write-downs is expected to be limited. HYBE anticipates that the effects of these preemptive structural improvements will lead to a significant increase in profitability starting this year.

The ripple effect of HYBE's label-centric business model in the global market has been proven through the case of KATSEYE. As of the fourth quarter of last year, KATSEYE surpassed 36 million monthly listeners on Spotify, recording the highest figure among all-girl groups worldwide. Notably, the title track "Gabriela" has been on the Billboard Hot 100 chart for 28 consecutive weeks, achieving long-term popularity. Recently, the group simultaneously placed two songs within the top 30, a feat unmatched by any girl group since Destiny’s Child. [Photo=HYBE]

  
 HYBE posted its highest annual revenue since its founding, with sales up about 18% from a year earlier. The company said its “multi-home, multi-genre” strategy aimed at global markets and strong growth in concert revenue drove the expansion. Operating profit fell year over year as HYBE reflected costs tied to upfront investment for mid- to long-term growth and changes to its profit structure.  
   
 On a consolidated basis, HYBE’s 2025 revenue totaled 2.6499 trillion won, led by performance results. HYBE held 279 global events last year — 250 concerts and 29 fan meetings — generating 763.9 billion won in performance revenue, up about 69% from the prior year.  
   
 HYBE said the momentum helped it climb five spots to No. 4 worldwide in Billboard’s “Top Promoter” category in the “2025 Boxscore Year-End Report,” placing it among the “big four.” Of the four K-pop acts listed in Billboard’s “2025 Top Tours,” three — j-hope, Seventeen and Enhypen — were HYBE Music Group artists, the company said.  
   
 Despite a broader adjustment in the album market, HYBE said it maintained its influence in 2025. On the annual Circle Chart, cumulative sales were about 19.6 million albums, with an estimated market share of about 30%. HYBE Music Group artists logged a combined 3.7 billion streams, and their share on the “Global Spotify 200” was 3%. Digital music accounted for about 37% of HYBE’s total recorded-music revenue in 2025.  
   
 Weverse, HYBE’s global superfans platform, turned profitable for the year after restructuring its revenue model and improving operating efficiency. HYBE said results were supported by adding more artists, upgrading e-commerce operations and expanding digital businesses. The company expects further improvement this year as BTS resume group activities and as e-commerce and digital businesses grow.  
   
 HYBE’s 2025 consolidated operating profit was 49.9 billion won, down about 73% from a year earlier. The decline reflected early-stage investment tied to new artist debuts and one-time costs from business restructuring.  
   
 HYBE cited debuts by multiple artists, including Japan’s aoen, South Korea’s CORTIS and Latin act SANTOS BRAVOS, which concentrated initial costs. HYBE said aoen’s debut single “The Blue Sun\_” topped Oricon’s daily chart, CORTIS became a million-seller in its first year, and SANTOS BRAVOS sold out a 10,000-seat debut concert, with 70,000 people watching online.  
    
 HYBE also reflected one-time costs tied to operational efficiency efforts. In North America, it is reorganizing to reduce volatility from a management-centered structure and shift toward a label-centered IP business model. After a conservative review of asset values aligned with the new structure, HYBE recognized about 200 billion won in impairment losses in nonoperating profit and loss in the fourth quarter, including in its management business. The company said the loss is an accounting item with no cash outflow. HYBE said the move was intended to improve accounting transparency and predictability, and that given HYBE America’s strengthened fundamentals, the risk of additional large write-downs appears limited. HYBE expects the effects of these steps to translate into a meaningful rise in profitability starting this year.  
   
 HYBE pointed to the global impact of its label-centered model through the example of KATSEYE. As of the fourth quarter of last year, KATSEYE surpassed 36 million monthly listeners on Spotify, HYBE said, the highest figure among girl groups worldwide. The title track “Gabriela” has charted on the Billboard Hot 100 for 28 consecutive weeks, and the group recently placed two songs in the top 30 at the same time — a first for a girl group since Destiny’s Child, HYBE said. Its first solo tour, “The Beautiful Chaos Tour,” sold out all dates, and per-capita spending on tour merchandise exceeded that of existing pop artists, the company said.  
   
 HYBE said it plans to expand its influence in the global music market this year. BTS are set to release their fifth full-length album, “Arirang,” on March 20. The group’s first full-member album in about four years will be followed by HYBE’s largest world tour to date, the company said. A schedule has been confirmed for 82 shows in 34 cities worldwide — the largest ever for a single K-pop artist tour — with additional dates in Japan and the Middle East to be announced later.  
   
 In South Korea, a new girl group is scheduled to debut this year. In North America, HYBE plans to launch a follow-up global girl group based on KATSEYE’s formula. It is also accelerating preparations for a local boy group project in collaboration with multi-platinum producer Ryan Tedder, a four-time Grammy Award winner. HYBE said it will also introduce new IP combining storytelling and music through the Alan’s Universe project, which has 100 million YouTube subscribers, and plans to run projects tailored to local culture in India.  
   
 HYBE also unveiled a new three-year shareholder return plan. It said it will introduce a “minimum dividend” guaranteeing at least 500 won per share, which it described as a first for a K-content company. HYBE will also change its dividend benchmark from net profit to consolidated free cash flow to better reflect cash generation and reduce volatility from noncash gains and losses. Under the new standard, HYBE plans to use up to 30% of free cash flow as return resources from 2025 through 2027.
